On this page

Introduction to Feluqa ​

Feluqa is an application platform and runtime built with Rust for enterprise backends, standalone workstations, high-stakes operations, tactical units, and defense-adjacent workloads (such as ground-side drone telemetry, sensor-fusion ingestion, and secure logistics).

The goal is to share one codebase across web, desktop, mobile, and IoT deployments, while adapting each build to its target environment.

By avoiding heavy runtime overhead and garbage-collection pauses, Feluqa aims to bring the performance and control of native software to business applications and field systems.

Feluqa is under development. Some capabilities are implemented; others described here are design targets. Each guide marks its implementation status so readers can tell the difference.

StatusMeaning
ImplementedAvailable in the current Feluqa release and covered by the documented baseline.
PartialSome foundations exist, and the page identifies what is missing.
TargetAn agreed design that is not yet fully implemented.
ExploringAn idea or working proposal that may change.

  • Taxonomy: learn the shared meanings of Application, Platform, developer kit (SDK), module, product, and other terms.
  • Architecture overview: see how source code, modules, build artifacts, runtime components, and deployment targets fit together.
  • Create your first application: see the planned path from project setup to a useful running application.
